headline: GOLD CHARGES TO $4,100: FIRST MONTHLY GAIN SINCE FEBRUARY — Japan Yen Intervention Hammers Dollar as FOMC Hold + 3 Hawkish Dissents Ignite Precious Metals
snippet: Gold held near $4,100 per ounce on July 31, 2026, on track for its first monthly gain since February as two catalysts converged: suspected Japanese currency intervention weakened the US dollar sharply, and the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75% on July 29 — over the objections of three hawkish Fed presidents who voted for an immediate 25-basis-point hike — reinforced the case for non-yielding assets. Spot gold rose 2% to $4,101.99 in the immediate aftermath of the FOMC announcement. For junior mining investors, a monthly close above $4,100 after the 28% drawdown from January's $5,596 all-time high signals recovering institutional sentiment — and with H1 gold equity earnings reports still digesting into valuations, the July close sets the tone for August. The 30-year Treasury yield simultaneously hit its highest level since 2007 as markets debated whether the Fed is falling behind the inflation curve.

headline: BUENAVENTURA Q2: GOLD UP 12% AT SAN GABRIEL RAMP, $4,342 REALIZED GOLD, $89.52 SILVER — Peru's Largest Miner Reports; Conference Call Today (NYSE: BVN)
snippet: Compañia de Minas Buenaventura (NYSE: BVN), Peru's largest publicly traded precious metals company, announced Q2 2026 results on July 31 showing 30,543 gold ounces from direct operations — a 12% increase year-over-year driven by the continued ramp-up at the San Gabriel gold mine — and consolidated silver production of 3.62 million ounces, up 2% year-over-year. Realized prices were $4,342 per gold ounce and $89.52 per silver ounce, with analyst consensus pointing to approximately $1.03 EPS on $610 million revenue. San Gabriel has been Buenaventura's long-awaited primary growth catalyst; the 12% YoY gold output increase confirms the ramp is proceeding on schedule. Management hosted a conference call at 11:00 AM ET on July 31. At $4,342 realized gold — well above the sub-$2,000 environment in which San Gabriel's economics were originally modeled — the cash margin expansion here is substantial.

headline: WARSH CALLS IT "THE FED'S GOOD FAMILY FIGHT" — 3 HAWKS DEMAND RATE HIKE; Gold Surged 2% as Hold Prevailed; September Decision Now Critical for Gold
snippet: The July 29 Federal Reserve decision to hold rates at 3.50%-3.75% was the most contentious FOMC vote of the cycle: Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis' Neel Kashkari, and Dallas' Lorie Logan all voted for a 25-basis-point hike — three simultaneous dissents, a rare display of internal division — and Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh publicly called it a 'good family fight' among central bankers. Money Metals Exchange journalist Mike Maharrey's analysis argues this dissent pattern, combined with Middle East energy-driven inflation and a Dow that fell 1,153 points on rate-hike fears, sets up a binary scenario for gold: if the Fed hikes in September, gold consolidates near $4,000; if it holds again, real yields compress and gold pushes higher. Gold's own 2% rally on hold day itself signals the market is pricing the 'hold wins' scenario — but the September FOMC is now the most important single date on the calendar for junior mining investors.

headline: ABRASILVER CLOSES C$50M BOUGHT DEAL FOR DIABLILLOS — Kinross Private Placement Adds Producer Endorsement; Argentina Silver-Gold Advances to Next Milestone (TSX: ABRA)
snippet: AbraSilver Resource Corp. (TSX: ABRA) closed its bought deal public offering on July 29, 2026, raising C$49.99 million through 3,401,000 shares at C$14.70 per share — with National Bank Financial, Beacon Securities, and Raymond James as bookrunners, Scotia Capital and TD Securities also participating. Concurrent with the bought deal, Kinross Gold Corporation subscribed to a concurrent private placement at the same C$14.70 price, adding institutional validation from a senior producer with an existing strategic focus on Argentina. Net proceeds will fund the advancement of the 100%-owned Diablillos silver-gold project in Argentina's Salta Province toward a revised PEA or prefeasibility study. With silver at $59+ and the Diablillos resource base sitting among the largest undeveloped silver deposits in the Americas, the oversubscribed deal at full exercise of the overallotment option signals the financing market is fully open for quality silver developers in 2026.

headline: GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS + DISCOVERY SILVER BOTH SURGE 10%+ IN ONE WEEK — Frank Holmes Names Top Outperformers as Q2 Earnings Accelerate Re-Rating
snippet: In his weekly Gold SWOT analysis at GoldSeek, US Global Investors CEO Frank Holmes highlighted DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) and Discovery Silver Corp. (TSX: DSV) as the standout equity performers of the week — each rising more than 10% in a single week. DPM's outperformance follows its record Q2 2026 free cash flow report and the continued market recognition of its Brevene South porphyry discovery at Chelopech, Bulgaria (713 metres at 2.52 g/t AuEq), which confirmed a fourth significant discovery for the company in the Western Tethyan Belt in three years. Discovery Silver's move reflects institutional accumulation ahead of catalysts at its Cordero silver project in Chihuahua, Mexico — one of the world's largest undeveloped silver deposits by ounces, which at current silver prices is an increasingly compelling development-stage NAV story. Holmes' broader point: as Q2 earnings confirm record operating leverage across the gold and silver mining sector, the institutional re-rating that has lagged physical metal performance is now catching up.

headline: MOTLEY FOOL: 2 RARE EARTH STOCKS TO BUY NOW, 1 TO SELL — After 81% H1 Surge, Analyst Grades the Sector; USAR CEO Change + China Processing Gap Are the Key Risks
snippet: A July 29 Motley Fool analysis grades the rare earth investment landscape after the sector's 81% H1 2026 rally, identifying two stocks worth buying at current prices and one to sell — framing each pick against the core structural tension: political tailwinds for domestic US rare earth supply chains are real, but China's dominant control of rare earth processing means that Western developers remain years from operational independence, and the current valuations embed expectations of government support that must eventually be validated by cash flows. The CEO transition at USA Rare Earth Inc. (USAR) — Barbara Humpton retiring October 1, succeeded by Thras Moraitis — is flagged as a management continuity factor in a pre-production company where leadership continuity at the Serra Verde acquisition integration is operationally critical. The investment framework the piece applies: prioritize companies with actual production or near-term first production, rather than those primarily reliant on political catalysts to reach milestones.

headline: GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%, INDIUM +26.5% — RARE EARTH BASKET AVERAGED +16.7% IN JULY as China Export Controls Compound Into Structural Price Floor
snippet: July 2026 delivered the strongest broad-based rare earth price surge since H1 2023, with the tracked basket of critical elements averaging a 16.7% monthly gain: germanium led at +27.8%, followed by indium at +26.5%, dysprosium at +25.4%, and terbium above +20%. The catalyst is China's ongoing export control regime — now covering germanium, gallium, antimony, and several heavy rare earths — which has made Western demand almost entirely inelastic: buyers cannot find alternative suppliers at scale, so price discovery is now happening almost entirely on the demand side. The longer-term structural driver is the continued expansion of permanent magnet demand from EV drivetrains, wind turbines, and AI data centre cooling systems — sectors where substitution is technically difficult and design cycle times span years. For TSX-V and ASX rare earth developers, July's price action validates the economic case for projects that were marginal at pre-2025 prices and increasingly compelling at current ones.

headline: URANIUM SPOT $86.60 (+21% YOY): KAZATOMPROM VOLUNTARY CUT BITES — AI Hyperscaler Nuclear PPAs From Meta and Microsoft Accelerate Demand Thesis
snippet: Uranium spot prices reached $86.60 per pound by late July 2026 — a 21% year-on-year increase — reflecting the combined effect of Kazatomprom's intentional 10% production cut to support price stability, a May 2026 logistics disruption at Cameco's McArthur River/Key Lake complex (flooding of the Smoothstone River Bridge, quickly resolved via an alternate route), and accelerating nuclear power purchase agreement announcements from hyperscalers. Meta and Microsoft have each announced multi-reactor nuclear PPAs in 2026, joining the earlier agreements by Amazon and Google, and 38 countries have pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050. Cameco Corporation (NYSE/TSX: CCJ) released Q2 2026 financial results on July 31 — the first major uranium producer quarterly report of the season — against a backdrop of a significant step-change in realized pricing: 2026 delivery guidance of 29-32 million pounds at $85-89/lb versus $62.11/lb realized in 2025.

headline: LITHIUM TRIANGLE STUMBLES: SQM + ALBEMARLE SLIDE ON EV DEMAND DOUBT — DRC First-Ever Lithium Exports to China Add New Supply Variable to Battery Metals Equation
snippet: Albemarle (NYSE: ALB) and SQM (NYSE: SQM) both declined in late July 2026, with Albemarle signalling caution on expansion plans and the broader Lithium Triangle complex facing questions about near-term EV adoption rates in Europe and North America. The structural backdrop has shifted: the Democratic Republic of Congo executed its first-ever lithium exports in June 2026 as Zijin Mining began shipments from its Manono project — targeting 30,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate equivalent for 2026 — under a preferential duty-free access agreement specifically structured to benefit Chinese buyers. This Zijin-controlled Congolese supply, arriving under a framework non-Chinese buyers cannot replicate, adds a new variable to the Western-hemisphere lithium supply picture. Albemarle Q2 2026 results are scheduled for August 5, 2026. For junior lithium developers on the TSX-V and ASX tracking their own feasibility economics, July's equity softness in the majors is a useful valuation check against macro assumptions.

headline: GOLD MINERS "TEEING UP" FOR RE-RATING — GOLDSEEK SWOT: 24.9% ROIC AT $4,700 GOLD Not Reflected in Current Equity Valuations; Q2 Records Close the Valuation Gap
snippet: Frank Holmes' weekly Gold SWOT analysis at GoldSeek argues that gold mining stocks are in a technical and fundamental 'tee up' configuration — with producer free cash flow yields, EV/EBITDA multiples, and price-to-net-asset-value ratios all at historically attractive levels relative to the spot gold price, even after Q2 2026's record earnings season. Holmes cites Scotia Capital data showing that at $4,700 gold, the weighted average Return on Invested Capital for major gold producers runs at 24.9% in 2026, 21.9% in 2027, and 19.7% in 2028 — ROIC levels that historically precede significant institutional capital rotation into the sector. The analytical observation: gold equity markets are still pricing producers as if gold is at $2,500, while the companies are generating cash flows as if gold is at $4,500. Q2 2026 earnings reports — including Agnico Eagle, Kinross, Endeavour, and Buenaventura all landing this week — are providing the hard data to close that gap.
